# maek

> maek is a zero-auth HTTP tunnel server. It exposes local applications
> at public URLs on this host - no account, no API key.

This server's base URL: __SERVER_URL__

## Expose a local app

1. Install the CLI:

   macOS/Linux:
     curl -fsSL __SERVER_URL__/_maek/install.sh | sh
   Windows (PowerShell):
     irm __SERVER_URL__/_maek/install.ps1 | iex
   Or with Go:
     go install github.com/gosuda/maek/cmd/maek@latest

2. Start an agent and keep it running:

   maek agent --server __SERVER_URL__ --alias my-app --target http://localhost:3000

   Flags: --alias (human-readable routing alias) | --desc (short description)
   | --target (local URL)

3. Verify registration - poll until your service appears:

   curl __SERVER_URL__/_maek/api/services
   -> [{"id":"my-app","alias":"my-app","connected_at":"..."}]

4. Your app is now public:

   - Stable browser URL: __SERVER_URL__/_maek/my-app
   - Header routing (curl/API): curl -H "X-Maek-Service: my-app" __SERVER_URL__/
   - Alias routing is also available at __SERVER_URL__/_maek/my-app

## Alias semantics

- IDs are assigned by the server from the Alias.
- The first active `my-app` gets ID `my-app`; duplicates get `my-app-2`, `my-app-3`, and so on.
- IDs are globally unique while active and are the canonical share target.
- Aliases may be shared by multiple active services.
- Alias routing selects the oldest active service; when it disconnects, the next-oldest service becomes active for that alias.
- If an Alias cannot produce a safe ID, the server falls back to a random ID.

## Protocol

- Agent and server negotiate a maek WebSocket subprotocol before starting the tunnel.
- A single agent connection may register multiple services.
- Yamux data streams carry a maek stream header with service ID and negotiated content encoding.

## Notes

- No auth anywhere. Closing the agent process closes its tunnels.
- Browser routes accept either the server-issued ID or an alias: __SERVER_URL__/_maek/<id-or-alias>
- Source: https://github.com/gosuda/maek
